title: Planning and SMART Goals Explained | Principles of Management Ep 15
description:
Why does a new shop need more than a wish? In this animated lesson, Ravi is opening a second Chai Corner outlet. His only plan is "sell more", and day one goes wrong: the milk runs out, nobody knows who opens the shop, and no one can tell if sales went up.

You will learn what planning means (deciding in advance what to do, how, when and who will do it), the 7 steps of the planning process (set objectives, develop premises, identify alternatives, evaluate them, choose the best, make supporting plans, implement and follow up), the 3 types of plans (strategic, tactical and operational), and SMART goals: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound. The SMART idea comes from George T. Doran's 1981 article in Management Review (his original letters were Specific, Measurable, Assignable, Realistic and Time-related). Ravi's wish becomes a SMART goal: sell 500 cups a day at the new outlet by March.

This is Episode 15 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.

In this video:
0:00 A second outlet, but no plan
0:20 What is planning?
0:33 The 7 steps of planning
1:10 Strategic, tactical and operational plans
1:29 SMART goals
2:03 Quick check
2:16 Recap
